reference.source: Stiehm's Immunologic Disorders / IUIS classification of inborn errors of immunity
clinicalPearls: Represents the most severe form of severe combined immunodeficiency, presenting in the neonatal period with overwhelming infection and failure to thrive
The defining laboratory triad is profound congenital neutropenia (agranulocytosis) unresponsive to growth factor, severe lymphopenia and sensorineural deafness
Both myeloid and lymphoid arms fail, so there is combined loss of T and NK cells with impaired B-cell function alongside the agranulocytosis
Sensorineural hearing loss is a distinctive extra-haematopoietic feature that separates it from other forms of SCID
The bone marrow shows a maturation arrest of the granulocytic lineage with preserved erythroid and megakaryocytic lines
Inheritance is autosomal recessive, from biallelic loss-of-function variants in AK2 (adenylate kinase 2)
It is a paediatric emergency requiring protective isolation, avoidance of live vaccines and only irradiated, CMV-negative blood products
Allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation is the only curative treatment and correction of the immune defect does not reverse the deafness
reference.pathophysiology: AK2 (adenylate kinase 2) is a mitochondrial enzyme that maintains the balance of adenine nucleotides in the intermembrane space and supports the energy metabolism needed for cell differentiation. Its absence causes energy failure and increased apoptosis in the leucocyte precursors that are especially dependent on this pathway, producing a maturation arrest of both the granulocytic and lymphoid lineages while erythroid and megakaryocytic development is largely spared. The consequence is congenital agranulocytosis combined with severe lymphopenia and defective adaptive immunity. AK2 is also required within the developing inner ear, which accounts for the associated sensorineural deafness.
additionalDifferentials: Typical T-B-NK- or T-B+ severe combined immunodeficiency
additionalInvestigations: Full blood count and differential showing agranulocytosis, lymphopenia and preserved red cells and platelets
Bone marrow examination demonstrating granulocytic maturation arrest
Lymphocyte subsets confirming absent or very low T and NK cells
Serum immunoglobulins and, in neonates, TREC-based newborn screening abnormalities
Audiological assessment for sensorineural hearing loss
AK2 gene sequencing for biallelic loss-of-function variants
redFlags: Neonatal sepsis or overwhelming infection in an infant with agranulocytosis and lymphopenia
Failure of neutrophil count to respond to granulocyte colony-stimulating factor
Signs of graft-versus-host disease after non-irradiated blood products
Complications of live vaccine administration in an undiagnosed infant
Progressive failure to thrive with intractable infection
reference.prognosis: Reticular dysgenesis is uniformly fatal in early infancy without treatment; allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation, ideally performed early, can be curative for the immune and myeloid defect, although the sensorineural deafness persists.
pitfalls: Mistaking the agranulocytosis for isolated severe congenital neutropenia and overlooking the lymphopenia
Giving live vaccines or non-irradiated blood products before the diagnosis is recognised
Failing to test hearing and missing the diagnostic association with deafness
Delaying referral for transplantation while pursuing infection control alone
Assuming successful transplantation will also correct the hearing loss
references: Stiehm's Immunologic Disorders in Infants and Children
IUIS Expert Committee classification of inborn errors of immunity
management: Pursue early allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation, the only curative treatment for the combined immune and myeloid failure
Protect against infection with strict isolation and broad antimicrobial prophylaxis covering bacteria, fungi, Pneumocystis and viruses while awaiting transplantation
Give immunoglobulin replacement, use only irradiated, CMV-negative, leucodepleted blood products, and avoid all live vaccines
Recognise that the agranulocytosis is unresponsive to granulocyte colony-stimulating factor
Provide audiological support including cochlear implantation, as the sensorineural deafness persists after transplantation
Offer genetic counselling, family screening and prenatal testing given autosomal recessive AK2 mutations, using newborn screening for early detection
Coordinate care through specialist paediatric immunology and transplant services
